conviction_note: The FY26 line was pre-announced on 12 Aug 2026 (Premier Retail sales $795.5m, underlying EBIT c.$176m, down from $183m), so tomorrow's release has almost nothing left to surprise on that line. What remains unknown is the first-weeks FY27 commentary, the final dividend and the Smiggle reset update. The only document-backed evidence on the first weeks is a read-through from Myer's 22 Sep release, and that release points both ways: August weak, then improving in September on Father's Day. I sized it at -0.5 and emitted -0.4, trimmed because the stock is already down about 17% since 11 Aug and the retail business is implied at roughly 2x EBIT after the Breville stake and cash, which leaves little room for further de-rating.
bar: Premier's own FY26 guidance: Premier Retail underlying EBIT c.$176m on unaudited sales of $795.5m, lodged 12 Aug 2026 (ASX idsId 03124208, https://www.asx.com.au/asx/v2/statistics/displayAnnouncement.do?display=pdf&idsId=03124208; PDF is RC4-encrypted and I did not read it directly; figures corroborated by https://ragtrader.com.au/news/solomon-lew-shutters-uk-dream-for-peter-alexander and https://www.tipranks.com/news/company-announcements/premier-investments-trims-fy26-guidance-exits-peter-alexander-uk-stores-to-refocus-growth). The closest is Lew's own claim of 'a clear plan to bring this brand [Smiggle] back to growth in FY27' (https://www.ragtrader.com.au/news/peter-alexander-sales-up-smiggle-faces-reset). The consensus quarters list is empty, so sizes are capped small.

findings.finding: Myer's FY26 release on 22 Sep 2026 disclosed its first 8 weeks of FY27: Myer Apparel Brands (Just Jeans, Jay Jays, Portmans, Dotti, Jacqui E, the specialty mall chains Premier sold it) comparable sales -5.9% and total sales -6.0%, Myer Retail comps +1.8%, and a 'material downturn' in June-July. Premier habitually gives first-N-weeks brand sales at its full-year result (FY25: Peter Alexander +9.2%, Smiggle -4.0% in the first 6 weeks), so the FY27 read tomorrow is likely soft, especially against Lew's promise to return Smiggle to growth in FY27.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: First-weeks trading has driven PMV's results-day reactions. 1H26 on 20 Mar 2026: -4.31% even though Peter Alexander's first 7 weeks were said to exceed the 1H trend. FY25 on 25 Sep 2025: -0.15% on PA +9.2% and Smiggle -4.0% with a dividend described as a surprise. FY24 on 25 Sep 2024: -9.09%. The 12 Aug 2026 guidance cut: -11.01%. So soft commentary on this name has been sold hard, and good commentary has not been bought.
findings.why_not_priced: PMV closed -0.88% on 22 Sep and -0.45% on 23 Sep, the two sessions after Myer's release: well inside its ordinary daily noise. Shorts sit flat at 1.27%. So nothing on the tape or the register reflects the Myer data being mapped onto Premier's first-weeks number. The mapping is a hypothesis: Premier's categories (sleepwear and gifting, kids' stationery) are not Myer's youth and women's apparel. That is why the size is small.
findings.independence: Same direction, different sources: Accent Group like-for-like sales -2% in its first 7 weeks of FY27 (search summary citing August 2026 reporting-season coverage; primary URL not retrieved, so it is not load-bearing). Premier's own 12 Aug statement that 2H26 conditions were 'very challenging, in particular during the latter months' (https://ragtrader.com.au/news/solomon-lew-shutters-uk-dream-for-peter-alexander). Cutting against it: Myer's same release says August weakness improved in September on Father's Day promotions, and Father's Day is a Peter Alexander gifting event (same investing.com source).

outside_window.finding: The 24-store Peter Alexander concession relaunch in Myer (Heads of Agreement) starts August 2027. Macquarie calls it GM-dilutive but EBIT-margin-expansionary. It is known and long-dated.
Macquarie expects the clearer read on Smiggle's reset product to come at the December 2026 AGM rather than at the FY26 result.

baseline_tension: The single small negative cuts against the positive priced lean (+0.95), which is mostly a squeeze prior on a flat 1.27% short. It agrees with the direction of the soft run-up (-5.3% over 20 days). A -17% de-rating since 11 Aug and a very low implied multiple on the retail business argue for a muted downside, so I emitted -0.4 against the -0.5 finding.
